package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of struts2-core contain a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in the HttpParameters class. Due to improper case-insensitive handling of HTTP parameter names, attackers can craft requests that bypass input validation and inject arbitrary commands into a code execution path. This allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server, posing a severe risk to any application using these versions.

execution_context.trigger: During HTTP request processing at runtime

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During HTTP request processing at runtime, the code performs case-insensitive matching of HTTP parameter names using equalsIgnoreCase, allowing crafted parameters to bypass validation and flow directly into a call to Runtime.getRuntime().exec with user-supplied input, resulting in arbitrary command execution on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code allows untrusted user input from HTTP parameters to reach a critical code execution sink (Runtime.getRuntime().exec) without proper validation or sanitization, due to the use of equalsIgnoreCase for parameter matching. This enables attackers to inject and execute arbitrary commands on the server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal secure coding practices require strict validation and sanitization of all user input, especially before passing it to sensitive APIs like Runtime.exec. The actual code fails to enforce these controls, allowing user-controlled data to dictate command execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of Runtime.getRuntime().exec may occur in controlled administrative tools or plugins, but never with direct, unsanitized user input from HTTP requests. In secure applications, any command execution is tightly controlled and not exposed to external input.
key_indicators: Use of equalsIgnoreCase for HTTP parameter name comparison
Direct flow of user-supplied input to Runtime.getRuntime().exec
Absence of input validation or sanitization before command execution
Command execution triggered during HTTP request handling

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious HTTP request with specially cased parameter names to exploit the case-insensitive comparison flaw in HttpParameters.
attack_chain.leads_to: Bypass of input validation and injection of attacker-controlled data into the code execution path

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable code path is triggered during HTTP request processing, passing the attacker-supplied input directly to Runtime.getRuntime().exec.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the server under the privileges of the Java process

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains remote control of the server, enabling actions such as data theft, lateral movement, or further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full system compromise, data exfiltration, or deployment of additional malware

behavioral_signatures: Inbound HTTP requests to .action endpoints with unusual or mixed-case parameter names designed to bypass case-sensitive filters
Unexpected invocation of Runtime.getRuntime().exec or similar process execution APIs during HTTP request handling in Java application logs
Unusual child processes spawned by the Java application server in response to HTTP requests
file_indicators: Presence of struts2-core versions 2.0.0-2.5.2 or 6.0.0-6.3.0.1 in dependency manifests such as pom.xml or build.gradle
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with crafted, mixed-case parameters targeting .action URLs
Outbound network connections initiated by the Java process to external or attacker-controlled infrastructure following suspicious HTTP requests
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor HTTP traffic for requests to .action endpoints with suspicious or mixed-case parameter names that could exploit case-insensitive matching. Audit application and server logs for unexpected process execution events (e.g., Runtime.getRuntime().exec) during HTTP request handling. Scan dependency manifests for the presence of vulnerable struts2-core versions. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes to HttpParameters.java or related files. Deploy runtime application self-protection (RASP) or web application firewalls (WAF) with rules targeting this exploitation pattern to block or alert on attempted attacks.
